newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf Atochem aims to boost international presence.
newsitem.headline: Elf Atochem aims to boost international presence.

text.p: Elf Atochem, the chemicals division of Elf Aquitaine, aims to boost its profits and sales through an expanded international presence.

Jacques Puechal told a news conference on Wednesday in Nashville, Tennessee, that the unit aimed to increase profits and make them more stable by using basic chemicals with different cycles, by increasing chemical specialties internally, by acquisition and by expanding its international presence.
In material prepared for the news conference, Elf Atochem said it had slightly lower 1996 sales at 53.8 billion francs ($9.3 billion) against 55.5 billion in 1995.
It said its operating profit was also lower at 3.7 billion francs, against five billion in 1995, but up on the 1.8 billion of 1994.
In 1996, Elf acquired the Findley adhesives business, making it the world's number four in adhesives.
Puech said that after a favourable climate in the first half of 1996, the second half had worsened with low plastic prices and a rise in petrol-based feedstocks.
He said economic growth in Europe was depressed at 1.7 percent in 1996, with a decline in building and construction and a slight increase in cars.
This translated into stagnating activities for Elf Atochem in Europe while speciality chemicals outside Europe increased by 13 percent.

Puech said that Elf Atochem's three basic chemical activities -- petrochemicals, chlorochemicals and fertilisers -- had different price cycles which could stabilise the overall result. He added that an increased geographical spread could limit the impact of regional recessions.
Elf Atochem aimed to concentrate in Europe its basic chemical activities while developing special chemicals worldwide by internal growth or by acquisition.
As an area for internal growth he singled out CFC substitutes, of which Elf Atochem produces 180,000 tonnes per year.
In 1997, the 134a unit at Calvert City will come on stream with an additional 18,000 tonnes per year. The plant took a $135 million investment.
Elf Atochem invested a total of 5.5 billion francs in 1996. With a cash flow of 5.1 billion and asset sales of 0.8 billion it was able to cut debt to 5.4 billion francs, or 21 percent of equity.
Another speciality for Elf Atochem is molecular sieves used to filter certain kinds of molecules out of compounds.
A 250-million-franc investment project at a production site for molecular sieves started at Honfleur, France at the beginning of this year while another at Mobile, Alabama, will start in mid-1998.
Elf Atochem is also investing $200 million in acrylic acids, including a US joint venture with Nippon Shokubai.
Puechal said that in 2005, only 25 percent of Elf Atochem sales would be in France, with 30 percent in the rest of Europe, 25 percent in North America and 20 percent in Asia and other regions.
In 1996, the breakdown was 31 percent for France, 38 percent for the rest of Europe, 19 percent for North America and 12 percent for Asia and the rest of the world.
-- Marcel Michelson, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.772 French Francs)
